name: Char

sections.heading: Logical layout
sections.text: Four-byte scalar storage in the current native layout. Surrogates and invalid scalar literals reject.

sections.heading: Construction and members
sections.text: Single-quoted literal; codepoint() returns its integer scalar value.

sections.heading: Protocols and ownership
sections.text: The Char value preserves its concrete semantic identity through bindings and arguments. Arithmetic/comparison does not grant I/O authority; console is an explicit effect. Only the documented comparisons and generic constraint profiles apply. A TypeId does not synthesize a user-defined Eq/Ord, clone or drop implementation.

sections.heading: Errors, limits and target
sections.text: Use x86_64 Linux System V ELF for the executed examples. Incompatible types reject before publication; bounds and ownership checks precede an invalid read, mutation or drop. Internal descriptor layouts are not portable ABI promises.

summary: One Unicode scalar value, distinct from a byte and Text.
